note: The single source of truth for what is left before Catch Comics launches. Edit this file, reload Launch Control. Re-verified against production and the production database on 2026-11-22; every gate and blocker below carries the date its claim was last checked. It replaces the 2026-09-26 readings, which had gone 57 days stale and several of which had become false.

targets.rationale: Both blockers closed on 2026-09-22 and the offers fix is already verified on production. Soft launch tomorrow gives the mobile fix one deploy and one night of soak. Public launch six days later is enough to see whether real shoppers search, click and buy — and short enough that it cannot quietly become another month.

verdict.because: Price comparison is not operating. Every stored retailer offer — 2,246 Travelling Man and 34 World of Books, 2,280 in all — was soft-deleted by the 30-day retention sweep at 03:00 on 2026-10-27, thirty days after the last verified refresh on 2026-09-26. No scheduled job can replace them: every retailer with a price feed carries scheduled_sync_disabled, and price_check.canonical_products has recorded no run since 2026-08-09. A shopper today sees a live eBay price and nothing to compare it against.
verdict.clearsWhen: A verified retailer refresh has written priced listings again, launch:health reports products at 2+ retailers above zero, and a real product page shows the same edition at two retailers.

blockers.title: Ship the eBay edition gate to production
blockers.why: Production is serving the wrong book as the cheapest offer. For Hellboy Omnibus Vol. 1, 7 of 8 eBay offers were a different book — Vol. 2, Vol. 4 and a B.P.R.D. title — and the page quoted "from £14.42" for a book that costs £19.36. A shopper following the cheapest offer bought the wrong comic. This is the one defect that breaks the site's whole purpose.
blockers.done: The Hellboy Omnibus Vol. 1 page on production lists only Hellboy Omnibus Vol. 1 offers, and npm run audit:ebay-relevance shows 0 rails emptied.
blockers.evidence: DONE 2026-09-22. Deployed and verified on production: /api/ebay for ISBN 9781506706665 now returns 2 rows, both Hellboy Omnibus Vol. 1, leading at £26.99 — the Volume 2, Volume 4 and B.P.R.D. rows are gone. Launch smoke 20/20 after deploy.

blockers.title: Confirm product pages do not scroll sideways on a phone
blockers.why: The 2026-09-01 review recorded every product page rendering 644px wide at a 390px viewport, on production, with the header search form overflowing. Most comic shoppers are on a phone. If it is real it is a serious mobile failure on the core journey; if it is stale it costs one test run to close.
blockers.done: A Playwright assertion at 390px proves documentElement.scrollWidth <= viewport width on home, search and a product page — or the overflow is found and fixed.
blockers.evidence: DONE 2026-09-22. CONFIRMED real, then fixed. tests/e2e/mobile-overflow.spec.ts proved the product page rendered 644px in a 390px viewport; the cause was the shared Navbar — a 170px shrink-0 UK block plus px-8 gutters that 390px could not fund. Now px-4 below sm, the country label hidden below sm (the flag still states the fact), and min-w-0 on the search so it can actually shrink. All three pages pass; the rest of Browser Trust unregressed.

blockers.title: Final smoke test — every launch surface reviewed, on production
blockers.why: Ten of the fourteen Smoke Test sections had never been reviewed, and the founder had spent weeks testing by hand. A launch needs one deep, honest pass over the whole customer journey — right comic, right edition, trustworthy offer — on the real site.
blockers.done: Every section reviewed with evidence; every P0/P1 found is fixed, deployed and verified on https://www.catchcomics.com.
blockers.evidence: DONE 2026-09-26 (deploy dpl_6W5h3YRHqg1vuDDXPv499WDa1FEM, commit dccf9ff). Found and fixed on production: wrong-book eBay offers (X-Men priced with Avengers vs X-Men: AXIS, Invincible Vol. 3 with Invincible Iron Man, Hellboy Omnibus Vol. 1 with a Monster Sized HC, Star Wars Vol. 3 with Darth Vader) and different printings mixed into ISBN-anchored pages; Price Comparison 11,898px down a phone; a 112px-wide price column on tablets. Also: search focus ring, search failure retry, clean share previews, the Watchmen chip. 114 checkpoints recorded in launch/operations/final-smoke-2026-09-26.md.

blockers.title: Put priced retailer offers back — the refresh button no longer can
blockers.why: The site has 0 priced listings. 2,280 were soft-deleted at 2026-10-27 03:00:46 UTC, thirty days after their last refresh on 2026-09-26, by the retention sweep working exactly as designed. Nothing refreshed them because Travelling Man and World of Books both carry scheduled_sync_disabled, so the hourly and 4-hourly crons skip them, and the manual run that used to cover the gap died 17 seconds in on 2026-09-26. The refresh itself cannot undo this: price-verify selects rows WHERE deleted_at IS NULL and scopes every update the same way, so with no active rows left there is nothing for it to refresh. Reviving the offers means clearing deleted_at on those rows or re-ingesting the retailer — both production data changes, and both yours to approve.
blockers.done: launch:health reports priced listings above zero and products at 2+ retailers above zero, and a real product page shows the same edition at two retailers.
blockers.evidence: Proven by running it, 2026-11-22 16:47 UTC: the read-only dry run (npx tsx scripts/price-verify-dryrun.ts --max-rows 2300) reported target rows 0 for Travelling Man and 0 for World of Books — 41 sitemap requests, 0 product requests, 0 rows written, 1.6 min. Database: 2,246 Travelling Man + 34 World of Books rows all stamped deleted_at 2026-10-27 03:00:46.263. Travelling Man still lists the flagship edition at £14.99 but shows Sold out, so some of those rows should not come back at all.

blockers.title: Release the sitemap split so the catalogue can be indexed
blockers.why: One sitemap of 136,296 URLs and 26.7 MB is over both the 50,000-URL and 50 MB limits, so search engines reject the file whole and none of the product pages is submitted through it. On a catalogue-first site that is the file that matters most.
blockers.done: robots.txt lists /sitemap.xml plus the four product chunks, each chunk loads, and Search Console accepts them.
blockers.evidence: Fixed locally on branch audit/launch-blockers and verified against the live catalogue: 4 chunks of 45,000 / 45,000 / 45,000 / 1,277 = 136,277 products, plus 19 static routes, none over the limit. Not released.

blockers.title: Release the ComicVine endpoint fix
blockers.why: PATCH /api/product/{slug}/comicvine-id is public — proxy.ts gates only /admin and /api/admin — and took an unconditional write. One request repointed any product at any Comic Vine volume, and that column drives the character tags, the issue grid and the cover.
blockers.done: A PATCH against a product that already has a ComicVine id leaves it unchanged, and the route is throttled.
blockers.evidence: Confirmed reachable without authentication on production 2026-11-22 (HTTP 400 for an invalid value, so nothing was gating it). Fixed locally on audit/launch-blockers: gap-fill only, 30/min per IP. Not released.

blockers.title: Decide what the homepage shows when there are no price finds
blockers.why: With 0 priced listings, /api/homepage-deals returns no cards and the homepage falls back to TOP_DEALS — ten hard-coded comics with hard-coded prices and RRPs, shown under "Price finds today" and labelled only "Sample prices" in 11px grey. Six invented prices are the first thing a collector sees. That is a design decision, not a code fix, so it has been left exactly as it is.
blockers.done: The founder has chosen what that rail shows with no live data, and the homepage reflects it.
blockers.evidence: Observed on production 2026-11-22: the rail rendered "Price finds today / Sample prices" with Absolute Batman Vol. 1 £29.99, Amazing Spider-Man Vol. 1 £13.99, One Piece Vol. 1 £6.99 and three more. /api/homepage-deals returned no cards on 10 of 10 samples at 16:43 UTC, having returned 12 at 14:05 and 16:40 — the cached copy is inconsistent.

claudeContext:
I'm launching Catch Comics (https://www.catchcomics.com), a UK comic discovery and price-comparison site. Comic database first, price comparison second.

Stack: Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, Tailwind v4, TypeScript strict, Prisma 5 on Neon Postgres, hosted on Vercel (branch main auto-deploys), images on Cloudflare R2.

Launch state as of 2026-09-22: production smoke 20/20, Browser Trust passing, both launch blockers closed. Soft launch 23 Sept, public launch 29 Sept. Retailer prices come from Travelling Man (2,246 listings) plus live eBay; Amazon is affiliate-only with no price API (Rainforest retired 2026-07-13) and the Creators API returns AssociateNotEligible.

Hands-off without explicit approval: OffersTable and the pricing layer, /go affiliate redirect and click logging, prisma/schema.prisma, lib/search scoring and SQL, next.config.ts remotePatterns, sitemap/robots/structured data, .env.local.
claudeClosing:
Write me the exact Claude Code prompt required to inspect, implement, test, commit, push and production-verify this task.

Keep it bounded and launch-focused. Do not invent additional work. Do not touch the hands-off list without saying why and asking first.

quickActions.note: Both run through the local action bridge on 127.0.0.1:8319 that the Command Centre launcher already starts. Fixed arguments, no shell, single-flight locks — nothing on this page can pass anything to the child process.
